questions.q: At $\mathbf{w}_{old} = [1,\ 2]$ the gradient is $\nabla f = [2,\ -4]$. With $\eta = 0.15$, what is $\mathbf{w}_{next} = \mathbf{w}_{old} - \eta \nabla f$?
questions.explain: $\eta\nabla f = [0.3,\ -0.6]$, so $\mathbf{w}_{next} = [1 - 0.3,\ 2 + 0.6] = [0.7,\ 2.6]$. $[1.3, 1.4]$ adds the gradient (walks uphill); $[0.7, 1.4]$ mishandles the minus sign of the negative component; $[-1, 6]$ forgets $\eta$.

questions.q: Why does gradient descent move along $-\nabla f$ rather than $\nabla f$?
options: $\nabla f$ always points to the global minimum, so the minus sign is just a convention
$-\nabla f$ has a larger magnitude than $\nabla f$
$\nabla f$ is zero everywhere except at the minimum
$\nabla f$ points in the steepest **uphill** direction, so its negative is steepest downhill
questions.explain: The gradient (orange dashed line in the lab) points uphill; the green arrow $-\nabla f$ is the descent direction. Both have the same length.

questions.q: In the topographic map, how does the gradient relate to the white contour lines (lines of equal loss)?
options: It crosses them at a right angle
It always points to where they are densest
questions.explain: Moving along a contour line does not change the loss, so the direction of steepest change must be perpendicular to it.

questions.q: On **Lumpy Terrain**, the ball often stops in a shallow dip instead of the deepest one. Why?
options: The learning rate $\eta = 0.15$ is too large for this terrain
Gradient descent only uses the local slope, so it settles in whichever dip is nearby
The gradient is computed incorrectly on non-convex surfaces
The ball runs out of steps before reaching the bottom
questions.explain: Each step only follows the local downhill direction; once the slope is zero in a dip, the steps vanish. On the Convex Bowl there is only one dip, so every start reaches the deepest blue. $\eta = 0.15$ is small enough for both terrains.
